## Changes
- **A No AI Training page for your book.** Click + beside the Front Matter's heading and choose No AI Training to add a page saying the book isn't to be used to train generative AI. It goes after the Copyright page, starts with standard wording that you can change, and is printed under its title in every export that has the front matter. No project has it unless you add it.
## Fixes
- **Foolscap starts with the New Project window again.** With no project to reopen, it was showing the standard Open window instead. Open Existing… and Open Recent are in the New Project window if a project is what you're after. - **Add Comment and Add Bookmark are dimmed when they have nothing to mark.** With the insertion point away from any word, Add Comment still appeared in the Insert menu and the text's Control-click menu, and only made an alert sound. Add Bookmark did the same on an empty line. Both still work with nothing selected when there's a word or a paragraph to go on.

## Changes
- **Your name and contact details follow you.** If you're signed in to iCloud, what's in Settings › Writer is now the same on every Mac you use: change it on one and the others follow. The newest change wins, and your other settings stay with each Mac. If you already have different details on two Macs, the first to open this version sets them for both, so check Settings › Writer afterwards. - **Footnotes show as numbers, and a click opens them.** A note's words no longer appear among the text, so View › Show Footnotes and Hide Footnotes are gone. Click a note's number to read or change it, or hold the pointer over it to read it. Find still looks in footnotes: when it finds words in one, the note opens with them chosen. A snapshot still shows each note's words, so that you can see what's changed in them. Your notes are saved and exported as they always were.
## Help
- **Sending a paperback to the printer.** The Paperback PDF page has a new section, Sending it to the printer, for when the PDF is made: get the ISBN first and export again so the copyright page shows it, give KDP or IngramSpark the same trim size, paper and bleed as Paperback Settings, make the cover to the size the Export sheet gives, then check every page in KDP's Print Previewer and order a proof copy. Choose Help › Foolscap Help and look under Paperback PDF.
## Fixes
- **Writing Tools no longer damages footnotes.** Rewriting text with a footnote in it could change the footnote's words and turn it into ordinary text, showing OBJ boxes. Now footnotes leave the text you've chosen while Writing Tools works, so a sentence is rewritten as a whole, and each goes back after the word it followed, or at the end of the sentence if that word has gone. Images, tables, citations, cross-references, breaks and words with a comment or bookmark are left as they are, and if a change would still damage one, Foolscap takes it back and says so. - **The inspector's chosen tab shows its icon again.** On macOS 27, the tab chosen at the top of the inspector was a plain blue block with no icon, because the icon was drawn in the same blue as the tab's background. It now shows in white, so you can see which tab is open. Nothing changes on macOS 26. - **Restoring from a backup now always saves what it restored.** Restoring just after making changes could show the backup's words in the window while the project on disk kept the words being replaced, so they came back the next time it opened. It now saves the backup's words every time. - **Saving on two Macs while they can’t reach each other now works as it should.** macOS could ask which version to keep instead of Foolscap putting them together, and choosing one took the other out of the project. A scene changed on both could also lose one version with no snapshot. Foolscap now puts them together itself: the newer text stays, the older is kept as a snapshot, and an alert tells you which is which. "Not synced" also no longer flashes up while this happens. - **Foolscap now says when a project didn't open.** The Open window can occasionally close without passing the project on, and then nothing happened. Now an alert tells you, so you can try again.

## A steadier iCloud status
A small fix for projects kept in iCloud Drive.
- **No more brief "Not synced".** iCloud sometimes reports a problem for a moment as a project opens, then clears it, and the status bar showed "Not synced" for that moment. Now it says so only when the problem lasts a few seconds, as it already did for "Uploading to iCloud…".

## Getting ready for iCloud
This version starts the work on keeping a project in iCloud Drive and writing in it on more than one Mac. Projects are now saved a little differently, ready for it.
- **Keep projects in iCloud Drive.** Settings has a new General tab: set New projects to iCloud Drive, and the save panel opens in iCloud Drive's Foolscap folder. Move a project you have already with File › Move To…. While iCloud is uploading or downloading a project, or can't sync it, the status bar says so, and a project that isn't on this Mac yet downloads in a window before it opens. See Help › Keeping a project in iCloud.
- **Each Mac remembers its own place.** A project opens where you left off on the Mac you're using: the same scene, place in the text, split editor and open folders. On a Mac it's new to, it opens where you last left it on any Mac. - **A project open on two Macs keeps up.** If your Macs share a project through iCloud Drive or Dropbox, changes saved on one now come into the other as they arrive, without reopening it, and the status bar says which Mac they came from. When both Macs changed the same paragraph of a scene, your text stays and the other Mac's is kept as a snapshot, and Foolscap tells you. See Help › Getting started › Working on more than one Mac. - **Earlier versions can't open projects saved by this one.** Once you save a project in this version, an earlier Foolscap says it was made by a newer version. Update Foolscap on each of your Macs before opening your projects there.

## Test versions expire
From this version on, each test version of Foolscap expires about three months after it's made, so old copies don't stay in use. Updating before then keeps everything as it is.
- **Two weeks before**, the status bar at the bottom of a project's window says when, as in "Expires 28 January". Click it for more, or to check for updates. - **Once expired**, Foolscap says so when it opens, and the status bar says **Read-only**. Your projects still open, and you can read, search, print and export them, and copy from them. Changes aren't saved and new projects can't be made. Nothing in your projects is changed. - **Foolscap › Check for Updates…** gets the current version, which saves as usual. The alert and the status bar both have a button for it. - **Help**: Test versions, under Updates on the Settings page.
